description: Findings the Gerrit 'aireview' bot posted on each case's patchset, scraped from Gerrit. Treated as the reference set: a human-reviewed, already-actioned review from a more expensive model. Not ground truth in the strict sense -- it is neither complete nor guaranteed correct.

68339_ps2.subject: LU-12669 ec: serialize concurrent EC recovery readers

findings.message:
(minor) Only the -EAGAIN half of this leads to a restart. ll_file_io_generic() gates the restart on

    (!rc || rc == -ENODATA || rc == -ENOLCK || rc == -EIOCBQUEUED) && bytes > 0 && io->ci_need_restart

and -EINTR is not in that set, nor is it converted anywhere in cl_io_loop(). So the -EINTR path returns EINTR to userspace (or the short count if bytes were already transferred); it does not restart. Could the wording separate the two?

(minor) "instead of discarding them" doesn't match the code being replaced. The pre-image of vvp_io_ec_rd_end() only did cl_page_list_fini() on ec_page_list, which drops the cl_page refs; it never called cl_page_discard()/cl_page_list_discard(). The change is adding a ClearPageUptodate(), not replacing a discard.

(minor) This describes a hazard that can't happen, so the hunk it refers to has no functional effect - see the note on lustre/llite/file.c. Worth either dropping the sentence or rewording it as a deliberate decoupling from vvp_env_new_io() rather than a fix.

(minor) Placing cp_flags here costs more than the 8 bytes it needs. It lands between the bitfield group and the cp_kmem_index union, so on x86_64 struct cl_page goes 80 -> 96 bytes: 4 bytes of padding before cp_flags plus 4 more after the short union. Moving the field to the end of the struct (after cp_sync_io) gives 88 bytes instead.

cl_page is allocated one per cached page out of the cl_page_kmem-<bufsize> slab, so the extra 8 bytes scale with the client page cache.

(minor) vvp_env_new_io() returns &vvp_env_info(env)->vti_io unconditionally, so `io` at the top of restart: is already that same object - the old `io->ci_switch_ec_io` read happened before the memset, on exactly the storage the local now caches. cl_io_fini() at out: doesn't clear the bit either. So this hunk plus the one at the restart goto is a no-op today.

No objection to keeping it as insulation against vvp_env_new_io() changing, but then the comment shouldn't read as if it is fixing a live bug.

67980_ps2.subject: LU-20582 llite: fix statahead SFNAME pattern detection

findings.message: (typo) The field added is `lli_sa_sfname_cache`, not `lli_sa_fname_cache`. Worth matching the code so `git log -S` finds this later. Also "with 5 slot" -> "slots".
(typo) This bullet looks truncated: "If the entry is valid, a new." It also repeats the start of the bullet above it.

(suggestion) Writing `enable_statahead_sfname=1` silently switches `enable_statahead_fname` back on, and the fname store does the reverse. That is surprising for an admin who deliberately turned fname off, and it isn't mentioned in the commit message.

The coupling looks like it only exists because `sa_pattern_detect()` stops on the `-EACCES` that `sa_pattern_fname_detect()` returns when fname is disabled. Letting that case fall through to `sa_pattern_sfname_detect()` would keep the two knobs independent.

The guard is also redundant - `sbi->ll_enable_statahead_fname = val;` alone has the same effect.

(minor) `SA_DETECT_HIT` is never returned - `sa_sfi_detect()` yields 0, `SA_DETECT_MATCH` or a negative errno, and neither list nor sfname detect uses it. Is a caller meant to distinguish it, or can it go?

(defect) When this second precheck fails, `rc` still holds the `is_first_dirent()` result instead of `SA_DETECT_NONE`, and those values overlap the new enum: `LS_FIRST_DE` is 1 (`SA_DETECT_HIT`) and `LS_FIRST_DOT_DE` is 2 (`SA_DETECT_MATCH`).

For the dot case `sa_pattern_detect()` then reports a match even though no pattern bit was set, so `start_statahead_thread()` allocates the sai, installs the ctx and creates the kthread before hitting the "unsupported statahead pattern" CERROR at the `pattern & (LSA_PATTERN_SFNAME | LSA_PATTERN_LIST)` test. For `LS_FIRST_DE` it returns 0 but also skips the fname/sfname detectors, which the old `||` chain did not.

The window is `is_first_dirent()` itself, which does a readdir RPC. Two `ls -l` on the same directory is enough: only the first gets `lli_opendir_key`, the second still passes `dentry_may_statahead()`, and when the first closes its dirfd `ll_deauthorize_statahead()->ll_sa_reset_locked()` clears `lli_sa_enabled` under the second one.

An `else rc = SA_DETECT_NONE;` here would restore the old bool behaviour.

(minor) `inst` is assigned but never read - the body uses `$instance` from the caller's scope, so this helper only works when called from `test_123m()`. Passing it in and using `$inst` would be safer.

Two more nits nearby: `running_max` is missing from the `local` list, so it leaks into later subtests, and the error text on the `{1..20}` stat still says `{1..10}`.

68627_ps1.subject: LU-20689 utils: Support decimal (SI) size units

findings.message: (minor) Was "1Gjunk" really accepted before? The old code did `char next = tolower(*(end + 1));` and then `if (next != '\0' && next != 'i' && next != 'b') return -EINVAL;`, so 'j' made it fail. The forms that were silently swallowed are the ones whose first trailing character is 'i' or 'b' - "1Gi", "1Gb", "1Gigabyte". Using one of those as the example would also make the point that "1Gi" is now a hard error, which is a user-visible change of its own.

(minor) The shortfall looks off by a factor of 10^9. With `frac = 999999999999999999`, `frac_d = 10^18` and `size_units = 2^60`, `frac * size_units` wraps to 17293822569102704640 and the fraction contributes 17 bytes, so the old result was 1152921504606846993 against a correct 2305843009213693950 - about 1.15 EB (just under 1 EiB) short, not 1.1 GB.

(minor) This granularity does not match the code. layout_stripe_size_set() divides an extension size by SEL_UNIT_SIZE (1024) before checking it, and only then calls llapi_stripe_size_is_aligned(), which tests `size & (LOV_MIN_STRIPE_SIZE - 1)`. So EXT_SIZE has to be a multiple of 64MiB, not 64KiB - `-z 1M` and even `-z 64K` are rejected with "invalid extension size". Every in-tree user (sanity-flr, sanity-pfl, sanity-hsm, sanity-lfsck) uses 64M or larger, which matches. Should this say 64MiB?

(typo) This "256MB" is one of the spellings the patch set out to convert: DEF_CACHE_SIZE is `256 * 1048576`, so it is 256MiB. It now reads oddly right below the new paragraph that defines "1MB" as 10^6.

The suffix list on the line above ([KkGgMm]) is also missing T/P/E and the new B while you are here.

(style) Not a bug, but the skip text only restates the version. Something like "need client with decimal (SI) size unit support" says why the gate is there; same for the copies in 921b/921c/921d and sanity-hsm 608.

68468_ps1.subject: LU-19921 ptlrpc: do not unpack req in gssiam_extract_h_exp

findings.message:
(minor) If this does stay a separate change instead of being squashed, could it carry the origin so the bug can be tracked?

    Fixes: b3cfd7572798 ("LU-19921 target: verify GSSIAM tokens on the target")

(suggestion) This changes how a wire message's byte order is detected, and the failure it fixes only shows up for opposite-endian peers. A Test-Parameters: line asking for a cross-arch/interop run would document that the interop side was exercised, e.g.

    Test-Parameters: clientdistro=rocky9.5 clientarch=aarch64
(style) Can this be NULL? lustre_msg_buf() only returns NULL for n >= lm_bufcount or buflen < min_size, and buffer 1 was already checked to exist with min_size 0, so the branch looks unreachable.
